title: Execution of a template instruction
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Turing machine with Boolean input and $k$ work tapes, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $\theta$ be a template for $M$, let $e$ be a record of eleven natural-number register values, and let $p\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume that the label assigned as the successor of $\theta$ is the label that begins its per-template increment phase. From the label for $\theta$, with registers initialized to those specified by $e$, input position $p$, and any output word $o$, the counter program reaches the label assigned after $\theta$ in at most the length of $\theta$'s operation sequence plus three steps, still at input position $p$. Its registers are those specified by $e$ with the instruction counter increased by one and, when the template's initial-step flag is false, the preceding-cell counter also increased by one; its output is $o$ followed by the bits obtained by executing the template's operations using the initial register values.
